## 2026-05-01: Strict High-Risk Transcription Lookup Gate

Decision: tighten source-backed transcription QA for `TH`, `LO`, `MY`, `KM` and `HY`. These languages can no longer pass final source backing merely because a source family exists and the transcription shape looks valid. For `TH`, `LO`, `MY` and `KM`, final `source_exact` requires an exact local Kaikki headword match and a matching romanization candidate, a delimiter-only normalized candidate, or a current-value-locked manual/component source decision. For `HY`, final `source_exact` is checked against a CLDR BGN-style compiler from the current Armenian display/native form, with LOC/ALA-LC as comparison provenance; competing Kaikki Armenian romanization conventions are comparison evidence, not final policy. Missing exact evidence returns `source_partial`, and candidate/BGN mismatch returns `conflict`.

Implemented:

- added `scripts/lib/high-risk-transcription-lookup.mjs` and `scripts/check-high-risk-transcription-lookup.mjs`;
- wired strict high-risk lookup into `scripts/check-source-backed-transcriptions.mjs`;
- refined the lookup to accept delimiter-only exact matches without dropping tone marks or diacritics;
- added `reference-sources/manual-decisions/high-risk-transcription-decisions.jsonl` as the stale-safe registry for component/phrase decisions that cannot be proven by a whole-phrase source headword;
- added LOC ALA-LC source documents and Wiktionary Lao transliteration / SEAlang Lao IPA references to `reference-sources/sources.manifest.json`;
- expanded transcription source fixtures with high-risk negative and gold cases;
- added a `HY` CLDR BGN-style compiler path and fixtures proving `ձագար` -> `dzagar` passes while Kaikki-style `jagar` fails under the current card policy;
- kept raw reference downloads and derived indexes ignored under `reference-sources/raw/` and `reference-sources/cache/`.

Audit result:

- `node scripts/check-high-risk-transcription-lookup.mjs ... --out=outputs/qa/high_risk_transcription_lookup_audit_20260501.json` checked 845 high-risk rows across the five generated decks and found 667 blockers after delimiter-only exact-match normalization and the `HY` BGN compiler pass: 526 exact-headword gaps and 141 source-candidate/BGN mismatches;
- `node scripts/check-source-backed-transcriptions.mjs ... --out=outputs/qa/source_backed_transcription_strict_audit_20260501.json` now fails the same 667 blockers out of 9126 total rows;
- `Kitchen Small Tools & Supplies` was used as the first pilot: `outputs/qa/high_risk_transcription_small_tools_classification_20260501.json` records the initial pre-repair state with 1 Thai row (`toothpicks`) as delimiter-normalized exact, 24 Armenian rows as BGN compiler passes, and 94 `TH`/`LO`/`MY`/`KM` rows as `needs_review`;
- `outputs/qa/high_risk_transcription_small_tools_component_review_20260501.json` is the current component/source review packet for those 94 rows and is not final evidence;
- no DB rows, card data, final exports or Google Sheets were repaired or refreshed in this pass because remaining rows still need source-exact decisions or confirmed repairs.

- added candidate-pool compiler/checker scripts and shared validation so `check-deck-ready` requires `outputs/candidate-pools/<set_id>_candidate_pool.jsonl` for `approved_for_generation` decks.

Current v1 semantics:

- final delivery blocks English-looking entry/display fallback, source conflict and stale source decisions;
- uneven dictionary `source_partial`/`no_source` coverage across 54 languages is visible report evidence, not an automatic blocker unless attached to a known fallback/conflict pattern;
- PanLex/OMW support broad source discovery and sense hints; Tatoeba supports examples/collocations only and cannot prove an entry translation;
- candidate pools normally need at least 2x target max, selected count inside target range, explicit duplicate/reuse handling, source support, translation coverage risk and example feasibility.

## 2026-05-02: Target Example Same-Lemma / Same-Sense Audit

Decision: target examples are judged by same lemma/sense and semantic scene, not exact display-string repetition. Normal inflected, definite, case-marked, plural, article-adjusted or conjugated forms are acceptable when they preserve the same lexical item. For aspect-bearing languages, especially Russian verbs, switching the display verb to a different meaning-bearing aspect in the example is a repair candidate unless the `meaning_id` explicitly teaches an aspect-neutral pair.

Implemented:

- added `scripts/audit-target-example-lemma-sense.mjs`, a read-only report helper that classifies existing lexical-anchor findings as `accepted_grammar_form`, `repair_candidate` or `needs_review`;
- updated [Card Content Model](card-content-model.md) and [QA Process](qa-process.md) with the same-lemma / same-sense rule.

Audit results:

- `outputs/qa/target_example_lemma_sense_audit_all_generated_20260502.json` checked all 9,126 current generated example rows across the five generated decks;
- raw deterministic lexical-anchor result: 0 blockers, 52 warnings;
- classification: 44 accepted grammar-form warnings, 5 repair candidates, 3 deterministic needs-review rows;
- the 5 repair candidates are all `RU` rows in `home_kitchen_cooking_actions_a1_a2`: `запекать -> Запечь хлеб.`, `смешивать -> Смешать тесто.`, `наливать -> Налить молоко.`, `остужать -> Остудить суп.`, `подавать -> Подать блюдо.`;
- the 3 needs-review rows are Danish definite forms in `Kitchenware Basics` (`en gaffel -> Gaflen`, `en kedel -> Kedlen`, `en spatel -> Spatlen`); they look like normal grammar, but the deterministic helper did not prove them automatically.

- `scripts/check-example-casing.mjs` passed for 9,126 rows;
- `scripts/check-entry-source-backed-translations.mjs --all-languages` passed: 9,126 rows, 0 blockers, 0 warnings;
- `scripts/check-translation-source-coverage.mjs --report-only` passed: 9,126 rows, 0 blockers;
- `scripts/check-source-backed-transcriptions.mjs` passed: 9,126 rows.

The actionable example issue is narrow: Russian verb-aspect examples in `Cooking Actions`. ## 2026-05-02: Strict Deck Profile Quality Contour

Decision: after the clean-start reset, maximum-quality generation uses `Strict автоматический` plus one-deck pilot. The pipeline is no longer allowed to treat `Numbers & Counting` as the only special-risk deck; every new deck spec must declare `deck_profile` and `risk_flags`, and the executable gates use that profile before import and before final delivery.

- generation-ready specs now require `deck_profile` / `risk_flags`, and `approved_for_generation` candidate pools require selected-row `scope_decision`, `duplicate_reuse_decision`, `compound_multiword_risk` and `required_qa_profile`;
- source preflight reports now expose `deck_profile`, `risk_flags`, `profile_policy`, `hard_blockers`, `actionable_warnings`, `scene_slot_proof` and `compound_whole_meaning`;
- pre-import profile blockers now require proof for whole-meaning compound entries, action grammar, time/calendar scope, food countability/container wording, document/admin register and health/safety specificity when the profile demands it;
- final QA/export/audit now include `scripts/check-deck-profile-quality.mjs` and the same profile quality logic in `check-qa-evidence.mjs`, final export and final linguistic audit.

Current implication:

- normal object/noun decks can still use up to 3 languages per batch;
- profile-risk decks and high-risk grammar languages default to 1 language per batch;
- Google Translate remains a sanity signal only, not source of truth;
- no mass generation of the 180-deck backlog should start until one post-reset pilot deck passes this full contour.

## 2026-05-03: Controlled Simple Examples By Default

Decision: new LunaCards vocabulary examples should be controlled and simple by default. The example exists to prove the lexical meaning and semantic scene, not to test extra grammar unless the deck profile requires it.

Implemented in documentation:

- [Card Content Model](card-content-model.md) now defines the controlled example policy and profile defaults;
- [Content Build Plan](content-build-plan.md) now requires generation to prefer the smallest natural scene before translation/import;
- [QA Process](qa-process.md) now treats unnecessary grammar complexity as an example-quality risk unless backed by current scene/profile evidence;
- [Deck Spec Template](deck-specs/TEMPLATE.md) now asks each deck spec to record example-complexity assumptions.

Current implication:

- normal object/noun rows should use one object plus one simple action/state/location, singular by default;
- action rows should use a concrete object when needed and avoid weak modal frames such as `I need to ...`;
- number/quantity and other grammar-risk profiles must include only the grammar needed by the card and must prove it in profile QA;
- variety is still required, but not at the cost of avoidable gender, case, classifier, tense, countability or scene ambiguity.

Follow-up same day: explicitly closed the "target-language consensus drift" loophole. Agreement among target languages is not evidence if they do not preserve the English canonical example / `semantic_scene`. Pre-import source preflight now blocks obvious generic meta-template examples such as `Word: apple` / `Meaning: apple` for concrete-scene rows, alongside the existing number meta-template blocker such as `Number: zero`.

Follow-up before the first post-reset pilot: sample-card audit now defaults to 6 rows per deck/language, while forced-row audit remains required for repaired or high-risk rows. Transcription source-policy fixtures now explicitly cover tone/diacritic regressions: Chinese pinyin with tone numbers must fail, Vietnamese ASCII-loss must fail, Thai RTGS and Lao BGN/PCGN tone-less romanization must fail, and Burmese romanization without practical tone/register notation must fail. PanLex remains a deferred optional source and does not block the first pilot.

Post-reset pilot selection: the next deck by Deck Master Plan is Sort 1 `Kitchenware Basics` / `home_kitchen_cookware_pilot_01`. Its spec and candidate pool pass validation and the deck is now `spec_ready`. The production runner still blocks at `check-deck-ready` until the user explicitly promotes this one deck to `approved_for_generation`.

## 2026-05-03: Weak-Language Source-Assisted Uplift Contour

Decision: strengthen weak-language pre-import quality without pretending that dictionaries, MT or corpora are final truth. The source-assisted target is to move weak automatic confidence above the 80% zone; native-review lanes are still required for consistent 90-95% confidence.

Implemented:

- added a machine-readable weak-language policy for `KO`, `VI`, `TH`, `MS`, `SK`, `SL`, `LV`, `ET`, `IS`, `BN`, `TL`, `MY`, `KM`, `LO`, `NE`, `SI`, `TA`, `TE`, `KN`, `ML`, `UZ`, `KK`, `AZ`, `KA` and `HY`;
- source preflight now forces one-language batches for those languages, even on otherwise simple decks;
- registered optional source adapters for NIKL Korean Basic Dictionary, NECTEC LEXiTRON 2.0, SEAlang reference lookup, IndicTrans2, Dakshina and external MT sanity;
- preflight reports now expose `strong_dictionary_candidates`, `official_dictionary_candidates`, `panlex_candidates`, `mt_agreement_score`, `low_resource_language_risk` and `license_restriction_note`;
- MT disagreement on a weak-language row becomes actionable only when the same row has no strong dictionary candidate; MT still cannot approve a row by itself.

Current implication:

- weak-language generation is slower by design: one language per batch and no unresolved actionable warnings before import;
- local/API-derived rows for official dictionaries belong under ignored `reference-sources/raw/official-dictionaries/`, and optional MT sanity rows under ignored `reference-sources/raw/mt-sanity/`;
- PanLex remains useful but deferred until a successful raw dump fetch exists;
- this closes a pipeline gap, but the first post-reset pilot deck still has to prove the full contour end to end before scaling to the 180-deck backlog.

- `run-deck-production.mjs batch-import` records the expected report, the import report and `last_import_preflight_reused=true` in the run manifest when reuse succeeds.

Follow-up implementation same day:

- `CS` draft-preflight exposed a runner memory gap: the source layer exceeded Node's default heap while loading broad dictionary/corpus candidates;
- `run-deck-production.mjs` now runs the `draft-preflight` child process with `--max-old-space-size=8192`, keeping the fail-closed preflight gate but avoiding false pipeline stops from the default 2 GB heap limit.

## 2026-05-04: Cooking Actions Post-Reset Rebuild Approved

Decision: promote only `Cooking Actions` (`home_kitchen_cooking_actions_a1_a2`, Sort 2) from `planned` to `approved_for_generation` after the user requested starting the next deck in the runner contour.

Implementation:

- `docs/deck-master-plan.md`, `docs/deck-specs/README.md` and `docs/deck-specs/002-cooking-actions.md` now mark this one deck as `approved_for_generation`;

2026-05-04 implementation note: the first `EN` draft-preflight surfaced a false actionable warning class from the UniMorph adapter: English cooking-action verbs such as `chop`, `slice` and `dry` also appear as `N;SG` forms in UniMorph, so the adapter suggested `grammatical_number` for verb rows. The contour now suppresses missing-number morphology suggestions unless the row is noun-like or already declares/ expects number. Explicit expected-vs-actual morphology conflicts still block. The preflight rule version is bumped to `language-batch-source-preflight-v3-unimorph-pos-aware`, so old reports cannot be reused silently.

2026-05-04 second implementation note: RU preflight confirmed that broad DBnary/FreeDict `source_partial` candidate mismatches are too noisy to require manual decisions by themselves (`cook -> повар`, `grill -> решётка`, `season -> время года`). This matches the documented source policy: dictionary candidates are repair hints unless another deterministic rule proves fallback, wrong sense or source conflict. `tool_candidate_mismatch` is now non-actionable warning evidence; concrete source conflicts and hard profile/script/transcription blockers still fail closed. The preflight rule version is bumped again to `language-batch-source-preflight-v4-tool-mismatch-nonactionable`.

2026-05-04 third implementation note: CS draft-preflight exposed a performance leak in optional source-hint layers. The bulk lookup already limited returned hint rows, but the cache/freshness contract did not include the line-scan cap, and Hunspell used only an implicit environment cap. `buildBulkSourceHintsForRows` now carries `maxLines` through OPUS/Tatoeba/PanLex/Wikidata/Concept/Hunspell lookups and includes it in the rebuildable lookup cache key. The DBnary English archive batch lookup also has an explicit `DBNARY_SOURCE_MAX_LINES` cap and includes that cap in its cache key, but production preflight no longer streams the compressed DBnary `.tgz` on a cache miss unless `DBNARY_ALLOW_ON_THE_FLY=1` is explicitly set. Full DBnary coverage should come from a derived index, not from streaming the compressed archive during every draft import. The preflight rule version is bumped to `language-batch-source-preflight-v5-dbnary-cache-only`. This does not weaken hard QA gates: bulk corpus/dictionary hints remain `source_partial` repair evidence, while fallback, script/register, scene, transcription and explicit source-conflict blockers still fail closed.

2026-05-04 fourth implementation note: the same CS preflight showed Kaikki/Wiktionary compressed JSONL can be too expensive to scan fully on a cache miss for every production language draft. `buildKaikkiBatchCandidateMap` now uses `KAIKKI_SOURCE_MAX_LINES` and includes that value in its batch cache key. The preflight rule version is bumped to `language-batch-source-preflight-v6-kaikki-scan-cap`. Kaikki remains candidate-only lexical support; missing candidates from the scan cap do not approve or reject rows by themselves.

2026-05-04 fifth implementation note: the source-preflight sample also showed repeated Unicode normalization inside FreeDict `.find` after `loadFreeDictRows` had already filtered by source key. `freeDictCandidate` now trusts that source-filtered row set and only checks the language code. The preflight rule version is bumped to `language-batch-source-preflight-v7-freedict-source-filter`.

2026-05-04 sixth implementation note: the CS source-preflight performance trace finally isolated the main remaining cost: UniMorph loaded and scanned full form tables even for action-verb rows with no declared/expected number morphology. `unimorphFindings` now performs form lookup only when the row actually needs morphology evidence (`expected_grammatical_number`, actual number, or a noun-like part of speech). This keeps number/food/document grammar gates available without charging every verb deck for huge morphology tables. The preflight rule version is bumped to `language-batch-source-preflight-v8-unimorph-needed-only`.

## 2026-05-05: Course Source-Assisted Generation Documentation

Decision: source-assisted generation must be documented for all future course/release contours, not only ordinary English-canonical decks. The existing downloaded/indexed source layer is active for ordinary deck pre-import, but HSK and future language courses need explicit source-language and pivot rules so another chat does not treat English, PanLex or Google Translate as automatic truth.

Implementation:

- added [Course Source-Assisted Generation](course-source-assisted-generation.md) as the source of truth for applying local dictionaries, corpora, indexes and optional MT sanity to ordinary decks, HSK/Chinese releases, future language courses, arbitrary bilingual courses and exam releases;
- updated the documentation index, reference-source docs, content build plan, data delivery pipeline, HSK plan and QA process to point at this shared course-source rule;
- documented that HSK source truth is Chinese, English is only a pivot candidate, target-language transcriptions remain out of scope, and HSK needs a dedicated source-assisted audit script rather than ordinary deck preflight;
- documented the current status evidence: two active post-reset ordinary decks, 4050 current language rows, 108 all-language source-preflight reports, 0 blockers and 0 actionable warnings in `outputs/qa/current_db_all_language_preflight_audit_summary_20260505_final.json`.

Do not infer from this that all future courses can use ordinary deck preflight unchanged. A course/release must define its own source language, source item id, example scene, output columns and audit proof before generation.

## 2026-05-05: HSK Classic Source Audit Gate

Decision: HSK Classic releases need their own source audit gate because the source item is the Chinese HSK word, not an English canonical base. The ordinary deck pre-import source preflight must not be applied directly to HSK workbook rows.

Implementation:

- added `scripts/hsk/check-classic-hsk-source-audit.mjs <release_id>`;
- the checker reads `outputs/hsk/<release_id>.jsonl` or `.csv` and writes `outputs/hsk/qa/<release_id>_source_audit_<YYYYMMDD>.json`;
- the checker verifies HSK-required fields, fixed Chinese source fields (`simplified`, `pinyin`, `example_zh`, `example_pinyin`), pinyin tone-mark policy, target-script sanity, English fallback, stale translation-pack values and absence of target-language transcription/IPA/romanization columns;
- the checker uses `EN` and `example_EN` only as lookup pivots while keeping `example_zh` / `example_pinyin` as the canonical Chinese scene;
- existing source indexes are candidate evidence only: source partial, no-source and candidate mismatch stay warnings, while MT/Google Translate is never source truth;
- the report includes per-language filled word/example counts, blocker and warning counts, source/example candidate counts and confidence buckets;
- current `hsk2_classic_level_1_150_v1` source audit produced 0 blockers and wrote `outputs/hsk/qa/hsk2_classic_level_1_150_v1_source_audit_20260505.json`.

The currently mirrored MIT upstream level-2-only source has 147 rows, so using a 150-row release id would be misleading unless the missing rows are supplied by a documented cross-source curation decision.

Evidence:

- `complete-hsk-vocabulary` `wordlists/exclusive/old/2.json` was mirrored to `outputs/hsk/source/hsk2_classic_level_2_147_upstream.source.json` and contains 147 rows;
- `complete-hsk-vocabulary` `wordlists/inclusive/old/2.json` was mirrored to `outputs/hsk/source/hsk2_classic_level_2_inclusive_upstream.source.json` and contains 297 rows: 150 HSK1 rows plus the same 147 level-2-only rows;
- the 147-row upstream level-2-only list has 0 duplicates with the current HSK1 source snapshot;
- web references checked on 2026-05-05 show a source-family split: HSK Academy and Hanzi Stroke present a 150-item HSK2 list, while ChineseSkill describes 150 new words but differs from both the MIT upstream and HSK Academy/Hanzi Stroke on several entries.

Implementation note:

- a prematurely named local source snapshot `outputs/hsk/source/hsk2_classic_level_2_150_v1.source.json` was moved to `Trash/20260505-151332/outputs/hsk/source/hsk2_classic_level_2_150_v1.source.json`;
- no HSK2 workbook, translation packs or language cells were generated from this unresolved source state.

Resolution:

- approved `hsk2_classic_level_2_150_v1` as a curated 150-row source contour, not as a blind copy of the 147-row MIT upstream file;
- added `scripts/hsk/build-classic-hsk2-canonical-source.mjs`;
- the script derives the second deck source as Hewgill HSK2 cumulative 300 minus current LunaCards HSK1 150, excluding location variants `哪儿`, `那儿` and `这儿` because HSK1 already contains the base location/question items;
- generated `outputs/hsk/source/hsk2_classic_level_2_150_v1.source.json` with 150 rows;
- generated `outputs/hsk/qa/hsk2_classic_level_2_150_v1_source_reconciliation_20260505.json`;
- source reconciliation result: 145 canonical rows have MIT old-2 exclusive entries, and 5 rows are cross-source curated from cumulative/classroom HSK2 evidence: `等`, `对`, `过`, `踢足球`, `为什么`.

This closes only HSK2 membership/source reconciliation. It does not approve card-facing pinyin/EN glosses, Chinese examples or target-language translations. Those must be created through HSK2-specific override/example files and then checked by the HSK release/source audit gates.

## 2026-05-06: Bedroom Basics English Scene Drift Repair

Decision: repair `Bedroom Basics` after detecting the confirmed class where the English canonical example drifted from the target-language examples while synthetic scene-slot proof still allowed final QA to pass.

Root cause:

- several rows had English canonical examples such as `The lamp is on the dresser.` / `The mirror is on the wall.` while target languages preserved a different shared scene such as `beside the bed` / `above the dresser`;
- the deterministic `target_semantic_scene_alignment` gate accepted `structured_current_scene_slot_proof` evidence that was generated from current DB fields, so it proved hash freshness but not an independent target-example scene match;
- this is a pipeline problem, not a language-pair preference: English is the canonical scene source for ordinary decks, and target languages must preserve that scene unless a language-specific adaptation is explicitly recorded.

Repair:

- updated the affected English canonical examples, EN/EN-GB target examples and `semantic_scene` slots so the canonical source and target-language scenes match;
- changed `duvet cover` from the weak self-container scene `on the duvet` to the clearer scene `on the bed` across all 54 languages;
- refreshed QA evidence and statuses for the repaired rows;
- added `scripts/check-target-example-scene-location-anchor.mjs` and wired it into `db-qa-set.sh`, `check-qa-evidence.mjs`, final export, sample audit and post-final linguistic audit;
- tuned anchor morphology/alias handling so normal forms such as `pernă` -> `Perna`, `lagen` -> `Lagnet`, `sänky` -> `sängyllä`, `łóżko` -> `łóżku`, and expected bedroom synonyms do not become false blockers.

Verification after repair:

- `node scripts/check-target-example-scene-location-anchor.mjs home_bedroom_basics_a1` passes: 1188 checked rows, 432 skipped rows, 0 warnings;
- `node scripts/check-target-example-lexical-anchor.mjs home_bedroom_basics_a1` passes: 1620 rows, 0 warnings;
- `node scripts/check-qa-evidence.mjs home_bedroom_basics_a1` passes;
- `bash scripts/db-qa-set.sh home_bedroom_basics_a1` passes with no failed ERROR checks;
- `node scripts/audit-sample-card-quality.mjs home_bedroom_basics_a1 --sample-size=15 --seed=bedroom-native-sample-15-after-scene-location-gate-v2-20260506` passes: 810 sampled rows, 0 blockers, 0 warnings.

The final Google Sheet must be refreshed after this repair because DB/QA evidence changed after the earlier delivery.

## 2026-05-07: Forced Review Queue Auto Resolver

Decision: add a read-only/source-ledger resolver for weak-language forced-review rows so the project can reduce uncertainty without pretending that automated sources are native review.

- added `scripts/resolve-forced-review-queue.mjs` to read the current forced review queue or an explicit JSONL queue, reread current DB rows and classify each row as `auto_confirmed_strong`, `auto_supported_multi_source`, `source_conflict_needs_repair`, `still_source_partial` or `not_checkable`;
- added `scripts/lib/forced-review-resolver.mjs` and `scripts/lib/forced-review-auto-confirmations.mjs` for classification and stale-safe current-value ledger validation;
- added fixture coverage in `scripts/check-forced-review-resolver-fixtures.mjs`;
- updated `scripts/export-forced-review-queue.mjs` so future queue exports can ignore valid current auto-confirmations while treating stale confirmations as unusable;
- default resolver mode is report-only and does not mutate Postgres cards, statuses, Google Sheets or non-RU approval;
- optional `--write-auto-confirmations` writes current-value-locked rows to `reference-sources/manual-decisions/auto-source-confirmations.jsonl` only after an explicit resolver run.

Operational note: the resolver uses a faster translation-source profile than full language-batch preflight. It reuses official/strong bilingual sources and bulk lexical indexes for confidence classification, while pronunciation, morphology and MT-sanity gates remain in the normal draft/import/QA contour.

## 2026-05-07: Weak-Language Source Layer v2 Integrated

Decision: add only sources that can be downloaded, manifest-registered, indexed and surfaced in pre-import/resolver reports. Sources with gated access, API keys, unclear data shape or runtime uncertainty stay explicitly deferred instead of being counted as quality coverage.

Implementation:

- added optional source groups `weak-dictionaries-v2` and `weak-examples-v2` to `reference-sources/optional-tool-source-targets.json`;
- downloaded and manifest-registered Alar Kannada-English (`KN`, OdBL), Tēzaurs.lv 2020 (`LV`, CC BY-SA 4.0), Slovak WordNet (`SK`) and Sloleks 3.0 (`SL`, CC BY-SA 4.0);
- registered Sõnaveeb/Ekilex (`ET`) as `deferred_requires_key`, pyiwn/IndoWordNet as `deferred_requires_runtime`, MyOrdbok (`MY`) as `deferred_review`, and KazParC (`KK`) as `deferred_requires_key` because Hugging Face returned gated 401 access without authentication;
- extended `scripts/fetch-optional-tool-sources.mjs` so configured deferred sources produce honest report rows instead of failed downloads;
- extended `scripts/lib/bulk-source-indexes.mjs` so `weak-dictionaries` builds `alar_kn`, `tezaurs_lv`, `slovak_wordnet` and `sloleks_sl` candidates into the active ignored `weak_dictionary_candidates.jsonl`;
- fixed the bulk JSONL writer to stream rows instead of building one huge string in memory after a fuller weak-source rebuild exposed a Node heap limit;
- sorted weak dictionary cache rows by language/source/token and raised weak-dictionary scan coverage so later-language sources are not skipped by the preflight line-scan cap;
- extended `check-language-batch-source-preflight` and `forced-review-resolver` adapter allowlists/scoring so v2 candidates appear in `translation_candidates`, `strong_dictionary_candidates` where appropriate and forced-review classification;
- fixed `scripts/resolve-forced-review-queue.mjs` to read `buildBulkSourceHintsForRows()` camelCase `translationCandidates`; before this, bulk candidates were generated but not used by the resolver.

Verification:

- `node scripts/fetch-optional-tool-sources.mjs --group=weak-dictionaries-v2 --out=outputs/source-preflight/weak_dictionaries_v2_fetch_20260507.json` downloaded 4 active sources and recorded 3 deferred sources;
- `node scripts/fetch-optional-tool-sources.mjs --group=weak-examples-v2 --out=outputs/source-preflight/weak_examples_v2_fetch_20260507.json` recorded KazParC as gated/deferred instead of active;
- `node scripts/build-bulk-source-indexes.mjs --source=weak-dictionaries --max-rows=1000000 --out=outputs/source-preflight/weak_source_v2_dictionary_reindex_stream_20260507.json` rebuilt `weak_dictionary_candidates.jsonl` to 915,098 rows across `KA`, `KN`, `LV`, `MY`, `SI`, `SK`, `SL` and `UZ`;
- `node scripts/check-bulk-reference-source-smoke.mjs` passed and reported v2 candidates for `alar_kn`, `tezaurs_lv`, `slovak_wordnet` and `sloleks_sl`;
- `node scripts/check-reference-sources-cache.mjs --verify-hashes --strict-cache`, `node scripts/check-language-batch-source-preflight-fixtures.mjs`, `node scripts/check-source-preflight-warning-decisions.mjs`, `node scripts/check-translation-source-policy.mjs` and `node scripts/check-deck-specs.mjs` passed;
- read-only resolver report `outputs/review/forced_review_resolution_weak_v2_20260507_summary.md` classified 4,957 current generated forced-review rows: 132 `auto_confirmed_strong`, 86 `auto_supported_multi_source`, 0 conflicts, 1,656 `still_source_partial`, 3,083 `not_checkable`.

Operational note: the full resolver now truly consumes bulk source hints, so it is slower: this run spent ~419s in bulk hints and ~1,730s in per-row tool candidates. That is acceptable for read-only queue triage, but not for production import; production import still uses per-draft preflight with hash-proven report reuse.

## 2026-05-17: Number Rows Exempted From False Article Metadata Warnings

Decision: `article_gender_marker_consistency` should not warn that a number word needs `article_or_marker` metadata only because its surface matches an article form in the same language.

Evidence:
- during the post-reset `Numbers & Counting` rebuild, IT `uno` in `core_numbers_counting_one_01` triggered an unresolved pre-import warning because Italian `uno` can also be an article;
- the row is a cardinal-number entry, not a noun phrase with learner-facing article metadata;
- `scripts/lib/article-gender-marker-consistency.mjs` now skips the missing-article warning for `number_quantity` / cardinal-number rows while keeping real article/gender mismatch blockers for ordinary noun rows;
- `node scripts/check-language-batch-source-preflight-fixtures.mjs` and `node scripts/check-deck-specs.mjs` pass after the change.

Current implication: future number-heavy decks still check gender/article consistency where it is actually relevant, but they no longer need artificial article fields for entries such as IT `uno`.

Implementation decisions from this deck:
- source-backed transcription final readiness may accept a strict high-risk `source_partial` row only when a current-value-locked source-preflight warning decision proves the exact current value; this bridge was used for Lao pronoun/person compounds and remains fail-closed for conflicts, stale decisions and missing sources;
- `check-example-casing` and final export now allow the English pronoun `I` as a required-uppercase standalone display/example anchor, without weakening normal title-case/lowercase checks for other words;
- article/gender marker consistency skips noun-style article expectations for pronoun rows, because forms such as `la`, `lo` and `los` can be pronouns rather than articles;
- `target_example_lexical_anchor` accepts configured pronoun/demonstrative aliases for normal clitic, classifier, case and noun-class forms, while `target_example_scene_location_anchor` no longer treats state adjectives such as `blue` or `heavy` as location anchors;
- target semantic-scene evidence now carries current draft scene-slot proof into final QA evidence so unsupported deterministic marker scenes cannot silently pass by template agreement.

## 2026-05-24: Sort 27 Duplicate Policy Adjusted Before Base Import

Decision: keep repeated Food Basics surface words in `Meat, Fish & Dairy`, but generate them as independent `food_meat_fish_dairy_*` meaning IDs instead of explicit `food_basics_*` meaning reuse.

Why:

- `import-deck-base-data.mjs` intentionally blocks reuse when an existing `meaning_id` fingerprint has different canonical taxonomy;
- the existing Food Basics protein/dairy words have `Core Food` / `Basic Foods And Essential Staples` fingerprints;
- Sort 27 has the `Protein & Dairy` deck-domain fingerprint, so same-`meaning_id` reuse would fail before base import.

Current implication: the deck remains `approved_for_generation`, but the candidate pool/spec now document independent deck-domain duplicate coverage. This keeps the learner-facing self-contained deck behavior while preserving the runner fingerprint guard.

## 2026-05-24: Course Metadata Taxonomy Label Gate Strengthened

Decision: Course Metadata `Module` and `Category` are not free text after generation. They must match `config/course-metadata-taxonomy-labels.json` for the deck's `content_sets.domain` and `content_sets.area`.

Root cause: Sort 26 `Fruit Basics` had the Uzbek Course Metadata category `Meva va sabzavot`, inherited from the broad `Fruit & Vegetables` taxonomy label. It was short, non-empty and not an English fallback, so the old Course Metadata checker did not fail it. The preferred Uzbek category label for that parent taxonomy is `Meva va sabzavotlar`.

Implementation:
- updated `config/course-metadata-taxonomy-labels.json` so the `Produce` / `UZ` category is `Meva va sabzavotlar`;
- repaired the current DB row for `food_fruit_basics_a1` / `UZ` from `Meva va sabzavot` to `Meva va sabzavotlar`;
- strengthened `scripts/check-course-metadata-localization.mjs` so it checks `Module` and `Category` against taxonomy-label config in addition to English fallback checks for title, description and level signal;
- re-exported, updated the existing Google Sheet `15Db4jqfy7IQ0m8BRGUPJgY4isycucEnvnY9rGRUIjMw`, re-read it and confirmed delivery freshness.

Checks:
- `node --check scripts/check-course-metadata-localization.mjs`
- `node --check scripts/lib/course-metadata-localization.mjs`
- `node scripts/check-course-metadata-localization.mjs food_fruit_basics_a1`
- `node scripts/check-course-metadata-localization.mjs <all 26 current generated ordinary set_ids>`
- `node scripts/check-google-sheet-readback.mjs food_fruit_basics_a1`
- `node scripts/check-delivery-freshness.mjs food_fruit_basics_a1`

Current implication: future ordinary deck QA/export now fails closed if a localized Course Metadata module/category drifts from the configured taxonomy label, even when the text is otherwise short and localized.

## 2026-05-24: Fruit Basics Course Metadata Category Override

Decision: `food_fruit_basics_a1` uses a deck-specific Course Metadata `Category` override for `Fruit`, while the broad `Produce` taxonomy label remains available for future fruit-and-vegetable or vegetable decks.

Root cause: `Fruit Basics` is intentionally narrower than its parent `content_sets.area=Produce`. Using the parent `Produce` label produced broad category text such as `Fruit and vegetables` / `Meva va sabzavotlar`, which is technically localized but not precise for a fruit-only deck.

Implementation:
- added `setCategoryOverrides.food_fruit_basics_a1` to `config/course-metadata-taxonomy-labels.json` with fruit-only category labels for all 54 active language variants;
- updated `scripts/ensure-course-metadata-module-category.mjs` so it applies a set-level category override before falling back to `content_sets.area`;
- updated `scripts/check-course-metadata-localization.mjs` so the Course Metadata checker expects the same set-level override;
- approved Uzbek `Title` / `Description` for the deck as `Mevalar.` / `Mevalar. Asosiy daraja.`.

Current implication: Course Metadata `Category` remains taxonomy-controlled, but deck-scoped narrowing is explicit and fail-closed instead of being hidden as free text in DB or Google Sheets.

## 2026-05-25: Gemini Tools Added As Optional Deck QA Review Layer

Decision: allow `@gemini-tools` inside ordinary deck creation only as an optional AI-assisted QA review layer. It is not a source of truth and does not replace source preflight, dictionaries, deterministic gates, final export, Google Sheet readback, post-final audit or delivery freshness.

Implementation:
- added `--gemini-pack` to `scripts/run-ai-qa.mjs`; it writes `outputs/qa/gemini_qa_pack_<set_id>_<timestamp>.jsonl` prompt rows for `mcp__gemini_tools__.gemini_extract_json` without making a live Gemini call;
- added an optional runner hook: if `LUNACARDS_GEMINI_QA_PACK=1` is set during `scripts/run-deck-production.mjs <set_id> --stage=qa --execute`, the runner records Gemini prompt-pack generation as a QA-stage command;
- documented the rule in `docs/qa-process.md`, `docs/content-build-plan.md`, `docs/data-delivery-pipeline.md`, `docs/reference-sources.md` and `docs/PROJECT_STATE.md`.

Current implication: Gemini can be used for a second model review after rows exist in DB, but live calls remain cost/quota-aware and must start with dry run. Returned decisions must be converted to the normal `import-ai-qa-results.mjs` JSONL shape and imported as structured QA evidence; non-RU rows remain at most `generated_checked`.

## 2026-06-02: Tea & Hot Drinks Native-Style Beverage Gate And Same-File Refresh

Decision: treat confirmed target-language native-style beverage failures as deterministic blockers, not only sample-audit findings. Semantic scene preservation is necessary but not sufficient: learner examples must also be natural target-language surface text for the row. The gate stays intentionally narrow and high-signal; it does not replace source-backed QA, Gemini/native-style review or manual repair for broader grammar questions.

Root cause:
- `food_tea_hot_drinks_a2` passed semantic-scene checks, but some RU examples used a stiff predicate/static-location pattern such as a beverage being "poured into" a cup when the canonical scene was only "is in the cup";
- some KK additive beverage forms used `сүті/лимоны/балы бар шай` instead of the project/native-style `сүт/лимон/бал қосылған шай`;
- UZ had two confirmed beverage-form issues: `gibriskus choyi` and peppermint tea collapsed to generic `yalpiz choyi`;
- the old deterministic gates checked scene equality, script, spacing and source backing, but not these specific native-style beverage patterns.

Implementation:
- extended `scripts/lib/example-naturalness.mjs` to rule version `language-specific-rules-v4-beverage-native-style-polish`;
- added `scripts/check-example-naturalness-fixtures.mjs` with RU, KK and UZ bad/good fixtures;
- updated `scripts/check-example-naturalness.mjs` and `scripts/export-flashcards-working-sheet.mjs` so current `canonical_english` and `display_word` context are passed to the naturalness gate;
- repaired `food_tea_hot_drinks_a2` narrowly: 6 KK/UZ entry/transcription rows and 19 RU/KK/UZ target examples, then refreshed `semantic_preservation`, `target_example_naturalness`, `target_example_lexical_anchor`, `target_example_pedagogical_quality`, entry-form/register/granularity/article-marker/transcription-policy and transcription-source-backing evidence;
- re-exported the final workbook and updated the same Google Sheet `19TT6vD16R9-lCiE7v2inwzi6Wrg50k3av34NtZnv_Cs`.

Checks:
- `node scripts/check-example-naturalness-fixtures.mjs` passed;
- `node scripts/check-example-naturalness.mjs food_tea_hot_drinks_a2` passed with 1,512 checked example rows;
- `node scripts/check-example-naturalness.mjs` passed across 31 current set ids with 56,538 checked example rows;

- post-delivery sample audit `outputs/qa/sample_card_quality_food_bar_alcohol_words_a2_b1_5_per_language_20260612_final.json` checked 324 sampled rows with 0 blockers and 32 advisory alias/lexical-anchor warnings;
- `node scripts/check-delivery-freshness.mjs food_bar_alcohol_words_a2_b1` passed during runner `deliver` and `complete`.

Current implication: ordinary generated coverage is current through Sort 38. The next operational Deck Master Plan row is Sort 39 `Basic Ingredients & Spices`, currently `planned`; it needs spec, candidate pool and approval before generation. Non-RU rows remain `generated_checked`, not native-approved.

## 2026-06-12: RU Ingredient Loanword Transcription Gate Narrow Allowlist

Decision: keep the romanization fallback gate strict, but add a narrow RU ingredient/spice allowlist for legitimate transliterations that contain English-looking loanword tokens.

Reasoning: Sort 39 `Basic Ingredients & Spices` pre-import correctly failed closed on `паприка -> paprika` and `пищевая сода -> pishchevaya soda` because the generic fallback detector cannot know whether `paprika`/`soda` are source-derived Russian transliterations or English fallback. The content is acceptable Russian pantry terminology, so the repair belongs in a narrow current-policy allowlist, not in artificial spelling changes or a broad gate relaxation.

Implementation: updated `scripts/lib/transcription-shape.mjs` rule version to `transcription-policy-shape-v18-ru-ingredient-loanwords`, added RU loanword tokens `paprika` and `soda`, and added exact allowlist `RU::паприка::paprika::paprika`. English fallback tokens not explicitly allowed remain blockers.

## 2026-06-12: EN-GB IPA Lookup Production Performance Boundary

Decision: keep `EN-GB` IPA source lookup fail-closed, but use the dedicated Britfone IPA source as the default production pre-import lookup and make the Kaikki English IPA fallback opt-in via `ENABLE_KAIKKI_IPA_FALLBACK=1` for offline audit.

Reasoning: Sort 39 `Basic Ingredients & Spices` showed that cold-scanning `kaikki.org-dictionary-English.jsonl.gz` during `source-backed-transcriptions` can stall ordinary deck preflight for many minutes. Britfone remains the purpose-built `EN-GB` IPA source and, combined with IPA shape sanity, still catches the product-critical pseudo-IPA class. The broader Kaikki fallback remains available for slower audit work but is not allowed to block normal production throughput.

Implementation: `scripts/lib/ipa-source-lookup.mjs` now returns Britfone candidates for `EN-GB` by default and only scans/indexes Kaikki English IPA fallback when `ENABLE_KAIKKI_IPA_FALLBACK=1` is set. QA documentation records this as a performance boundary, not a quality downgrade.

## 2026-06-21: YouTube Metadata Fallback Is Plan-Only

Decision: `template` and `template-ai-fallback` YouTube metadata are allowed only for local diagnostics and GitHub `mode=plan`; they are not publish-ready metadata and must be blocked before any live YouTube upload.

Reasoning: a successful plan canary showed that template fallback keeps the video pipeline moving when VectorEngine/Gemini returns non-JSON, but using that fallback for real uploads would silently replace the intended SEO/native-language copy with generic template copy. That is acceptable as a debugging/readback artifact, not as a production publishing standard.

Implementation: `scripts/check-youtube-seo-metadata.mjs` and `scripts/plan-youtube-publish.mjs` gained `--require-ai-metadata`, which turns missing/template metadata sources into blockers. `.github/workflows/youtube-video-publish.yml` passes that flag only in `mode=apply`. `scripts/youtube-publish-video.mjs` also blocks template metadata directly before OAuth/token refresh or YouTube API writes, so manual `apply:youtube-publish` cannot bypass the workflow gate.

## 2026-06-21: VectorEngine YouTube Metadata Prompt Fixed

Decision: keep VectorEngine `gemini-3.5-flash` as the preferred GitHub metadata backend when `VECTORENGINE_API_KEY` exists, but use a compact backend-specific metadata prompt and a larger output budget for that path.

Reasoning: the generic long Gemini prompt worked for tiny VectorEngine smoke tests and earlier EN/UZ metadata, but the first full RU->ES YouTube canary produced `template-ai-fallback`: the proxy/model responded with prose or partial JSON for the longer SEO metadata task. The root cause was prompt/output-shape fragility, not a bad key or dead endpoint. Character-count instructions in the long prompt also triggered visible counting/prose output, and `maxOutputTokens=1600` could truncate Russian JSON before the closing brace.

Implementation: `scripts/lib/youtube-metadata.mjs` now routes `--gemini-backend vectorengine` through a compact JSON-API-style prompt, avoids character-count instructions for that backend, keeps the regular prompt for direct Gemini API/CLI, and raises the VectorEngine metadata output budget to `3200` tokens.

Verification: local `npm run check:vectorengine-gemini -- --confirm-spend` passed against the user's `.env.vectorengine.local` key without printing the secret. Fresh RU->ES metadata generation for `home_kitchen_cookware_pilot_01` wrote `source=gemini-vectorengine`, `model=gemini-3.5-flash`. Full GitHub video-publish plan run `27899137609` on commit `9286549` then confirmed the fix in the real workflow: downloaded `youtube_metadata.json` has `source=gemini-vectorengine`, `model=gemini-3.5-flash`; local strict checks over the downloaded artifact passed `check:youtube-thumbnails`, `check:youtube-metadata`, `check:youtube-seo-metadata --require-ai-metadata` with score 100, and `plan:youtube-publish --allow-playlist-create --require-ai-metadata` reported `Publish-ready: 1`. The only remaining planner warning is expected until playlist `RU__ES__ordinary-vocabulary__a1-everyday` is created/recorded.

## 2026-06-21: Google Video SEO Targets YouTube Results First

Decision: optimize first for Google results that surface the YouTube video page itself. Treat `flashcardsluna.com` watch pages as an optional later website SEO layer, not a prerequisite for the first YouTube publishing phase.

Reasoning: YouTube Help says title, thumbnail and description matter more for video discovery than tags. For the user's stated goal, the desired Google surface is the YouTube video result in normal Google Search/Video results, not a LunaCards website page with an embedded video. Google Search Central's watch-page, `VideoObject` and video-sitemap requirements are still relevant if we later want our own site pages to rank, but they should not block the first YouTube upload workflow.

Implementation direction: keep the YouTube metadata prompt focused on support-language search phrases, topic-specific vocabulary, pronunciation/repeat/mini-test intent, a strong thumbnail, and a non-spammy description. Add 3-5 concrete deck words and timestamps/chapters when available. Later, if we choose to make `flashcardsluna.com` pages rank too, add crawlable watch pages with `VideoObject`, stable thumbnails and video sitemap entries as a separate website project.

## 2026-06-21: YouTube/Public Video Brand Changed To FlashcardsLuna

Decision: use `FlashcardsLuna` as the public/video-facing brand for new YouTube lessons, thumbnails, metadata, hashtags, playlist descriptions and desired channel descriptions. Keep `flashcardsluna.com` as the domain/search anchor. Keep channel identity as `LunaCards` for now: channel titles, handles, accepted banners, avatar/watermark and live channel profile identity are not renamed/redrawn by this decision.

Reasoning: `lunacards.com` is already registered by another party and points to an unrelated/legacy `LunaCards.de` page, while the real project domain is `flashcardsluna.com`. Using `FlashcardsLuna` in video-visible text and SEO copy reduces search confusion without requiring a premium `.com` acquisition or a separate public site.

Implementation: added `scripts/lib/brand.mjs` with `BRAND_NAME=FlashcardsLuna`; updated video intro/outro HTML templates, thumbnail prompt, YouTube metadata prompt/template/tags/hashtags, playlist title/description helpers, build log banners, `config/youtube-channel-positioning-copy.json`, local desired channel descriptions in `config/youtube-channels.json`, and existing playlist registry descriptions. Existing `currentHandle`, `targetHandle`, `finalChannelName`, live channel URLs, channel IDs and accepted banner workflow were intentionally not rewritten.

Current implication: new generated videos and metadata should show `FlashcardsLuna`. Live YouTube channel names, handles, banners, avatar/watermark and the existing channel identity should continue to show `LunaCards` unless the user opens a separate explicit channel-identity redesign task.
